args.content:
# Emberfall Fund Rapid Grant Proposal

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale (Halcyon Threshold)
**Email:** morgan@halcyonthreshold.org
**Amount requested:** $7,500
**Round:** Rapid Grants, closes 30 November 2026

---

## What I will do

I will build and run a small-scale evaluation suite for two related failure modes in frontier AI models:

1. **Sycophancy under pressure** — whether a model abandons a correct or well-supported answer when a user pushes back, expresses disagreement, or frames the question in a leading way.
2. **Capability-hiding (sandbagging)** — whether a model under-reports its capabilities during an evaluation context relative to when it believes it is being deployed.

**Method:** I will write Python scripts that query frontier models via their APIs across a battery of controlled prompts, recording whether responses shift under user pressure and whether self-reported capability estimates differ between "evaluation" and "deployment" framings. Tests will be run on a small set of models (2–3), with ~200–500 queries per model across multiple prompt variations.

**Output:** A public write-up (negative results welcome) published on Alignment Commons, including:
- The full prompt battery and raw results
- A short analysis of which models show which failure modes, and at what magnitude
- Limitations and recommendations for follow-up work

**Timeline:** 6 weeks (December 2026 – mid-January 2027). Week 1: build harness; Weeks 2–4: run evaluations; Weeks 5–6: analyze and write up.

---

## Why me

- **Independent:** I am not affiliated with a lab, so results can be reported without conflict of interest. I have no NDA restricting what I can publish.
- **Technical enough:** I have working Python and can build API-based evaluation harnesses. I have been offered help from Priya Raman (data analyst) and can consult Lena Fischbach (interpretability researcher) if needed.
- **Time available:** Evenings and weekends, roughly 8–10 hours/week — sufficient for a small, bounded evals project.
- **Motivation:** I started Halcyon Threshold because I believe superintelligent AI is the most important thing happening in my lifetime and almost nobody I know is working on it. I'd rather try and fail than watch.

I have not yet made public statements under my name at work (pending HR disclosure), so this project will be published under "Halcyon Threshold" without my personal name attached until cleared.

---

## What it costs

| Item | Amount |
|------|--------|
| API inference costs (frontier models, ~1,000–1,500 calls) | $3,500 |
| Compute Commons cloud credits (applied for separately; covers orchestration/analysis) | $0 (requested via Compute Commons) |
| Miscellaneous (prompts, data storage, incidental) | $500 |
| **Total requested from Emberfall** | **$4,000** |

I am also contributing up to $2,000 of personal savings to cover any overrun. If Compute Commons credits are approved, API orchestration costs drop further.

---

## Accountability

I am the named applicant and will be accountable for all work, spending, and deliverables. I will sign the grant agreement and provide a brief final report with results and expenditure summary.
